city_center.name: Eastern Market (Detroit) + the Detroit River
city_center.landmark: Eastern Market, one of the largest historic public markets in the US (Saturday market since 1891); the Detroit River and Great Lakes; Michigan fruit belt to the west
city_center.notes: Detroit's Eastern Market is one of the oldest and largest year-round public markets in the country, running a major Saturday market. Michigan's fruit belt (west Michigan lakeshore) supplies cherries, blueberries, and apples. sources: en.wikipedia.org Eastern Market, Detroit; easternmarket.org.

cultural_notes: Detroit's Eastern Market is one of the oldest and largest year-round public markets in the US, with a major Saturday market dating to 1891 -- a civic food anchor (source: en.wikipedia.org Eastern Market, Detroit; easternmarket.org)
metro Detroit (Dearborn) holds one of the largest and most established Arab-American communities in the US, a major food-culture identity (source: general demographic framing, publicly documented)

Michigan's fruit belt along the west-Michigan lakeshore is a top US producer of tart cherries and blueberries, with a strong apple crop -- Great Lakes fruit is the regional produce story (source: Michigan fruit production framing, publicly documented)

Pewabic tile (a Detroit art-pottery tradition) adds a teal-glazed accent to the city's brick fabric; Meijer and Kroger are the metro grocers (source: Pewabic Pottery framing; chain regional footprint)
